# One sshd-session (connection multiplexing) holds several masters; the session shells
# are its children. A root-owned privileged monitor holds nothing we need.
self 610
user 0 root
user 1000 alice

proc pid=1 ppid=0 uid=0 comm=systemd
proc pid=500 uid=0 comm=sshd exe=/usr/bin/sshd args="sshd: /usr/bin/sshd -D [listener] 0 of 10-100 startups" deny=fd,exe
proc pid=590 ppid=500 uid=0 comm=sshd-session args="sshd-session: alice [priv]" deny=fd,exe
proc pid=600 ppid=590 comm=sshd-session exe=/usr/lib/ssh/sshd-session args="sshd-session: alice@pts/1,pts/2,pts/7" ptmx=7:1,9:2,11:7
proc pid=610 ppid=600 comm=zsh tty=pts/2 tpgid=610 loginuid=1000
proc pid=620 ppid=600 comm=zsh tty=pts/7 tpgid=620 loginuid=1000

expect check tty=pts:2 start=610 euid=1000 => start personal sshd
expect check tty=pts:7 start=620 euid=1000 => start personal sshd
expect holder pts=7 start=620 => pid=600 via=ancestor class=remote comm=sshd-session
# a pts held by nobody visible below a denied sshd-session: comm fallback
expect check tty=pts:8 start=610 euid=1000 => start personal sshd
expect holder pts=8 start=610 => pid=590 via=commfallback class=remote uid=0
